title: Paul Surrenders His Rights for the Gospel

questions.question: Paul asserts his freedom and apostleship by asking, "Have I not seen ____?"
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:1 (ESV): "Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are not you my workmanship in the Lord?"

questions.question: Paul says that even if he is not an apostle to others, at least he is to the Corinthians, for they are the ____ of his apostleship in the Lord.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:2 (ESV): "If to others I am not an apostle, at least I am to you, for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord."

questions.question: Do we not have the right to take along a believing ____, as do the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:5 (ESV): "Do we not have the right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas?"

questions.question: Paul asks if he and who else are the only ones who have no right to refrain from working for a living?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:6 (ESV): "Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no right to refrain from working for a living?"

questions.question: Paul uses human analogies to argue for the right of financial support. Which of these is NOT an analogy he uses in verse 7?
options: Who makes a weapon at his own expense?
Who serves as a soldier at his own expense?
Who plants a vineyard without eating any of its fruit?
Who tends a flock without getting some of the milk?
questions.correctAnswer: Who makes a weapon at his own expense?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:7 (ESV): "Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard without eating any of its fruit? Or who tends a flock without getting some of the milk?"

questions.question: Paul appeals to the Law of Moses, quoting: "You shall not muzzle an ox when it ____."
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:9 (ESV): "For it is written in the Law of Moses, 'You shall not muzzle an ox when it treads out the grain.' Is it for oxen that God is concerned?"

questions.question: If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap ____ things from you?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:11 (ESV): "If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?"

questions.question: Nevertheless, Paul says he has not made use of this right, but he endures anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of what?
options: the faith of the new converts
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:12 (ESV): "Nevertheless, we have not made use of this right, but we endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ."

questions.question: In the same way, the Lord commanded that those who proclaim the gospel should get their living by the ____.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:14 (ESV): "In the same way, the Lord commanded that those who proclaim the gospel should get their living by the gospel."

questions.question: Paul says he would rather die than have anyone deprive him of his ground for boasting. For if he preaches the gospel, that gives him no ground for boasting. Why?
options: For necessity is laid upon me. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
Because I merely pass on what I have received.
For the Lord gives the utterance and the power.
Because I was chosen against my will.
questions.correctAnswer: For necessity is laid upon me. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:16 (ESV): "For if I preach the gospel, that gives me no ground for boasting. For necessity is laid upon me. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!"

questions.question: What is his reward then? That in his preaching he may present the gospel ____.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:18 (ESV): "What then is my reward? That in my preaching I may present the gospel free of charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the gospel."

questions.question: For though I am free from all, I have made myself a ____ to all, that I might win more of them.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:19 (ESV): "For though I am free from all, I have made myself a servant to all, that I might win more of them."

questions.question: What famous phrase summarizes Paul's adaptability in ministry found in verse 22?
options: "I have become all things to all people, that by all means I might save some."
"I am weak with the weak, strong with the strong."
"To the Jew I became as a Jew, to the Greek as a Greek."
"I am all things to all men, that I might run the race."
questions.correctAnswer: "I have become all things to all people, that by all means I might save some."
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:22 (ESV): "To the weak I became weak, that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, that by all means I might save some."

questions.question: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? So run that you may ____ it.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:24 (ESV): "Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? So run that you may obtain it."

questions.question: Every athlete exercises self-control in all things. They do it to receive a perishable wreath, but we an ____.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 9:25 (ESV): "Every athlete exercises self-control in all things. They do it to receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable."

key_verse_text: To the weak I became weak, that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, that by all means I might save some.
